 GUWAHATI-22, P.S.-DISPUR, DIST- KAMRUP (M), ASSAM  VERSUS  THE STATE OF ASSAM  REPRESENTED BY THE PUBLIC PROSECUTOR, ASSAM Advocate for the Petitioner : MR. D GOSWAMI,

 BEFORE  HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE ROBIN PHUKAN  ORDER Date : 13.09.2024

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard Mr. D. Goswami, learned counsel for the applicant.

Also heard Mr. K.K.
Parashar, learned Addl.
Public Prosecutor for the State respondent.

2. This application under Section 438 Cr.P.C. is preferred by applicant, namely, Imtiaz Anwar, who has been apprehending arrest in connection with Dispur P.S. Case No.2497/2022 under Sections 420/468/471 IPC, for grant of Page No.# 2/3 pre-arrest bail.
3. It is to be noted here that the above-noted case has been registered on the basis of an FIR lodged by one Punya Devi Narayan, on 24.11.2022.

The essence of allegation made in the aforesaid FIR is that one Debajit Nath along with one Ajay Kumar Sharma and Pankaj Biswas manufactured forged registered instrument of General Power of Attorney, being Serial No.5646 and prepared a forged Imtiaz Anwar vs The State Of Assam on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119696236/
1 Deed, vide No.1139, dated 05.03.2022 and created false and fabricated Deed of Sale document No.25478 and No.20542, dated 02.07.2022 with the help of Sub-Registrar, Kamrup (Metro) and thereafter, grabbed her land.
4.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Mr. Goswami, learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is innocent and no way involved with the offence alleged in the FIR, except that he has connection with one Debajit Nath,
who is the principal accused here in this case, and that he was granted the privilege of interim pre-arrest bail, vide order dated 11.06.2024, but, due to some inconvenience, he could not appear before the I.O., for which this Court, vide order dated 19.07.2024, was pleased the recall the order dated 11.06.2024, and that the applicant is ready to cooperate with the investigating agency and therefore, it is contended to allow the application.

5. On the other hand, Mr. Parashar, the learned Addl. Public Prosecutor has produced the case diary before this Court and submits that the materials, so far collected in the case diary, are inadequate to show the complicity of the applicant with the offence alleged in the FIR.
However, Mr. Parashar submits that in some other cases, his complicity is there as reflected in the case diary.

6. Having heard the submissions of learned Advocates of both sides, I have gone through the application and the documents placed on record and also perused the case diary with the assistance of Mr. Parashar, learned Addl.
Public
Page No.# 3/3 Prosecutor.

7. In view of the materials collected so far in the case diary and in view of the submissions of learned Advocates of both sides, custodial interrogation of the applicant seems to be not warranted here in this case and therefore, this Court is inclined to allow the application.
9.

Accordingly, it is provided that in the event of arrest of the applicant in connection with Dispur P.S. Case No.2497/2022 under Sections 420/468/471 IPC, he shall be released on pre-arrest bail on executing a bond of Rs. 50,000/- with one surety of like amount to the satisfaction of the arresting authority.

The above privilege is, however, subject to the following conditions:
(i) The applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by the Investigating Officer as and when required;
(ii) The applicant shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer; and (iii) The applicant shall not leave the jurisdiction of the learned C.J.M., Kamrup(M),
Guwahati without prior permission.
10. In terms of above, this application stands disposed of.
11. Case diary be returned.
